F.the_resource_and_metric: Occupancy / resident SMEM+register footprint. The kernel is one grid loop over M with N hl.specialize'd (never tiled), so each program carries a register/SMEM-resident [M_BLOCK, N] fp32 accumulator (M_BLOCK*N*4 bytes) PLUS a [K_BLOCK, N] bf16 y-operand tile, both scaling with N. CONFIRMED IN GENERATED TRITON (compile-only, to_triton_code, no launch): default _BLOCK_SIZE_0=32 -> grid=ceil(131072/32)=4096 programs, acc=tl.full([32, _RDIM_SIZE_2], fp32); seed _BLOCK_SIZE_0=64 -> grid=2048 programs, acc=tl.full([64, _RDIM_SIZE_2], fp32). N is a constexpr _RDIM_SIZE_2 full-width axis reduced by tl.sum(.,1) on the accumulator (rides the accumulator, NOT an HBM row, exactly as the FACT_LANDSCAPE describes). Larger M_BLOCK at small N = more rows/program = fewer fatter programs = the occupancy the N-blind [32,32] default leaves on the table (1.4-2.7x default->best, RESULTS.md). The metric that moves: grid size halves and the resident fp32 accumulator width doubles as M_BLOCK 32->64.
F.the_predicted_boundary: M_BLOCK must SHRINK as N grows, because acc bytes = M_BLOCK*N*4 must stay under the per-program footprint budget (131072 B). VERIFIED IN CODEGEN at the crossover N=1024: [64,1024]*4 = 262144 B (> budget, > an SM's ~228KB SMEM) so the seed drops M_BLOCK to 32 where [32,1024]*4 = 131072 B fits exactly. Emitted seeds (arithmetic + codegen confirmed): N=256->M_BLOCK=64 (cap binds; prev_pow2 would give 128), N=512->64 (acc=131072 exactly = budget), N=1024->32, N=2048->16. The win regime is small N; the boundary is N=2048 where even M_BLOCK=16 strains SMEM and the family's advantage vanishes by design (RESULTS.md SMEM wall). The boundary is keyed on the same faithful quantity the lever branches on (n_extent*4 footprint), so the mechanism generalizes to the rule as written.
F.boundary_sanity_check: On the OTHER side of the boundary the win correctly disappears: at N=1024 M_BLOCK is forced to 32 (seed/best 0.96 still, but no more headroom to widen), at N=2048 to 16 and the win vanishes (SMEM wall) — the lever does NOT keep emitting a too-large tile, it tracks the budget down. The acc width sits at EXACTLY the budget (131072 B) for every N>=512, halving M_BLOCK each time N doubles — a clean monotone footprint law, not a per-shape fence.
F.the_property_to_key_the_fact_on: n_extent (the hl.specialize'd output width N = reduction.size_hint) feeding the resident fp32-accumulator byte footprint M_BLOCK*N*4 under ACC_BUDGET_BYTES. field_attribution.K_BLOCK: ATTRIBUTED. _BLOCK_SIZE_1=32 sets the K-loop trip count (tl.range(0,256,32) = 8 iters). Distinct from the default's 32 here BUT the default tile_k is also 32, so on the curriculum K_BLOCK is unchanged from default — it is a deliberate pin (min 16 by min_dot_size, clamp <=K), not an inert addition; it keeps K tiling sane while M_BLOCK varies.
